chunks: Yunus narrated from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about pre-emption (al-shuf'ah): for whom is it, in what is it, and for whom is it suitable? And is there pre-emption in animals, and how is it? He said: 'Pre-emption is permissible in everything, whether animal, land, or movable property, if the item is shared by two partners exclusively. If one of them sells his share, his partner has more right to it than anyone else. And if there are more than two, there is no pre-emption for any of them.'

key_terms.ٱلشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption, the right of a co-owner to buy out another's share

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on pre-emption (shuf'ah) for co-owners of property?
ai.summary: Transmitted via Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith establishes the permissibility of pre-emption (shuf'ah) across all categories of shared property—land, animals, and chattel—provided the partnership consists of exactly two parties. The restriction to two partners highlights a specific juristic interpretation within the Shia tradition, distinguishing it from other schools that may extend the right to multiple co-owners, thereby emphasizing the prevention of unwanted intrusion into a private partnership. This ruling underscores the Islamic legal principle of protecting existing co-owners' rights to maintain control over shared assets against external parties.
